requirement:
This project's CI generates Rustdoc for the workspace before building the book.
The published documentation includes both the book and that generated Rustdoc
site in the same GitHub Pages deployment under
{cite}`requirements.integration.ci`. The appendix contains a "Rustdocs" entry
opening the `trust_but_verify` crate's documentation under
{cite}`requirements.index.rustdocs`.
rationale:
The reviewed test adequately checks every obligation in `requirements.index.rustdocs.publication`. The test is `tests/rustdocs.rs#fn[rustdocs_ci_generates_workspace_site_before_building_the_published_book]`. I derived the obligations from the requirement text and mapped each to an assertion.

- **CI generates Rustdoc for the workspace before building the book.** The test parses `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and finds the step running exactly `cargo doc --locked --workspace --no-deps`. It finds the `mdbook build` step in the same `test-and-build` job. It asserts `docs < build`, so the workspace-wide Rustdoc step runs before the book build. If the step were removed, reordered, or narrowed to a non-workspace command, the `unwrap` on the position lookup or the ordering assertion would fail.
- **Book and Rustdoc go out in the same GitHub Pages deployment.** The test asserts that `build < upload`, where `upload` is the `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4` step. It also asserts that the artifact `path` is `book`. Together with the `book.toml` rustdocs import configuration (`path = "target/doc"`), this checks that the generated Rustdoc is imported into the one `book/` directory that is uploaded. Deploying only on `main` after the check jobs pass is the cited `requirements.integration.ci` obligation. It is context here and needs no test in this subject.
- **The appendix has a "Rustdocs" entry that opens the `trust_but_verify` crate's documentation.** The test takes the part of `md/SUMMARY.md` after `# Appendix` and asserts that it contains `[Rustdocs](./rustdocs.md)`. It asserts that `md/rustdocs.md` consists solely of the `:::{rustdocs}` / `:::` directive. It asserts that `book.toml` sets `preprocessor.habeas.rustdocs.crate` to `trust_but_verify` and `path` to `target/doc`. It also asserts that the habeas renderer command is configured, which is the book-side configuration the directive needs.

The cited `requirements.index.rustdocs` behaviors cover the preprocessor's import, error reporting, and link resolution. They are context only. The subject requires no test of them.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that the test would accept, and no acknowledged or unacknowledged gaps.

text: :::{req} rustdocs.publication
This project's CI generates Rustdoc for the workspace before building the book.
The published documentation includes both the book and that generated Rustdoc
site in the same GitHub Pages deployment under
{cite}`requirements.integration.ci`. The appendix contains a "Rustdocs" entry
opening the `trust_but_verify` crate's documentation under
{cite}`requirements.index.rustdocs`.
:::{req} ci

A GitHub Actions CI workflow MUST run, for pull requests and pushes to `main`, these checks: `cargo habeas coverage -- --locked --workspace` under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run`, `cargo test --locked --doc --workspace`, `mdbook test`, the autofix controller tests with `node --test .github/scripts/autofix.test.mjs`, and, in a separate job, the Symposium session-start hook smoke test `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`. It also builds the book as documentation under {cite}`requirements.index.render_only`, without requiring collected execution reports for rendering. On a push to `main`, only after every check job passes, it deploys the generated `book/` directory to GitHub Pages. The book MUST set `output.html.site-url` to `/habeas-codicem/` for project-site hosting.
::::{req} rustdocs
A book can import a generated Rustdoc site through its Habeas preprocessor
configuration:
```toml
[preprocessor.habeas.rustdocs]
path = "target/doc"
crate = "trust_but_verify"
`path` identifies the generated documentation directory relative to the project
root; `crate` selects the landing page at `<crate>/index.html`. A chapter
consisting of one closed, standalone `{rustdocs}` directive with an empty body
becomes a navigation entry into that crate's Rustdoc site. The directive opens
with at least three colons and closes with at least as many:
```text
:::{rustdocs}
The built book includes the imported site under `rustdocs/`, preserving its
pages, assets, search data, and links. Selecting the chapter opens the native
Rustdoc page in the same tab, with Rustdoc's own layout and navigation. Relative
links from book chapters to imported item pages resolve when the publication is
hosted under a URL prefix.
The build reports a readable error if the directive has no import configuration, the
configured directory, crate landing page, or any imported site file cannot be
read, the import fails, or an imported file would overwrite a book output file.
